activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence fits the archive gap?
activities.passage: The archive began digitising its photographs in stages. ___ This allowed staff to correct labels before adding more files.

options.text: The first stage was deliberately kept small.
Visitors preferred the printed catalogue.
The building has a new entrance.
The photographs show several rivers.

activities.explanation: A small first stage explains how staff could check labels before expansion.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence completes the shuttle paragraph?
activities.passage: The council introduced a shared shuttle for villages outside the town. ___ Older residents could reach the clinic without arranging a lift.

options.text: The route was designed around the most regular essential journeys.
The clinic has recently changed its colour.
The town owns several bicycles.
Most villages have narrow gardens.

activities.explanation: The route design explains how the shuttle produced the benefit in the following sentence.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence belongs in the office gap?
activities.passage: The new office layout reduced private rooms. ___ Staff reported that informal questions were easier to resolve.

options.text: It also placed project teams closer together.
The old building was made of stone.
Several staff brought plants.
The project ended in January.

activities.explanation: Closer teams explain why informal questions became easier despite fewer private rooms.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which option maintains the argument?
activities.passage: The scheme reduced waste in the catering department. ___ Other departments are now considering whether the same approach would work for them.

options.text: The team ordered smaller quantities more frequently.
The building serves lunch at noon.
The bins were painted last year.
Several visitors asked for directions.

activities.explanation: The sentence gives a concrete example of the waste-reduction approach.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence fits the design gap?
activities.passage: The report presents two possible designs. ___ The other is cheaper initially but may need more repairs.

options.text: The first uses stronger materials and costs more to build.
The report was printed in two colours.
The committee met on a Tuesday.
The building has a wide entrance.

activities.explanation: The first design must be introduced before the second is contrasted with it.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence completes the report?
activities.passage: The pilot attracted many volunteers but demanded more coordination than expected. ___ The organisers therefore revised the registration process.

options.text: Several people had registered through different channels.
The pilot took place beside a river.
The volunteers preferred blue badges.
The report included a photograph.

activities.explanation: Different registration channels explain the coordination problem and revision.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence belongs in the museum gap?
activities.passage: The first survey suggested strong support for the redesign. ___ The authors recommended a broader consultation before drawing a firm conclusion.

options.text: Most responses came from people who attended the public meeting.
The redesign included three new benches.
The council met in the afternoon.
Residents use the square in summer.

activities.explanation: The limited respondent group explains the recommendation for broader consultation.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence best completes the explanation?
activities.passage: The archive postponed the digital launch after finding inconsistent dates. ___ Accuracy was considered more important than speed.

options.text: Several labels would have needed correcting after publication.
The archive sells books at weekends.
The launch was advertised in the local paper.
The photographs were stored in boxes.

activities.explanation: The possible corrections justify the decision to delay for accuracy.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which option maintains the contrast?
activities.passage: The new timetable reduced delays on two routes. ___ The team has not yet examined the rest of the network.

options.text: Nevertheless, the result cannot yet support a network-wide claim.
For example, one route has a blue sign.
The station opened many years ago.
Passengers often carry umbrellas.

activities.explanation: Nevertheless introduces the limitation that the positive result is narrow.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence completes the comparison?
activities.passage: The first design has a lower purchase price. ___ The committee later selected the second after reviewing ten-year maintenance costs.

options.text: The alternative uses more durable materials.
The committee printed the plans twice.
The room was quiet during the meeting.
The supplier delivered on Tuesday.

activities.explanation: The durable alternative must be introduced before the later decision is explained.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence fits the gap in the article?
activities.passage: The rooftop garden lowered the building's summer temperature slightly. ___ The organisers are monitoring water use before expanding it.

options.text: That modest result is encouraging but not sufficient on its own.
The roof was repaired before the trial.
The building has a basement.
Several gardeners prefer roses.

activities.explanation: The sentence evaluates the small result and prepares the need for monitoring.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence belongs in the transport gap?
activities.passage: The course attracted more applicants after an evening option was added. ___ Attendance, however, remained steady.

options.text: The increase therefore shows interest rather than a proven completion benefit.
The classrooms were painted white.
The course had no application form.
Applicants always completed the course.

activities.explanation: The missing sentence interprets increased applications while the next sentence limits the conclusion.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence best completes the argument?
activities.passage: The policy increased recycling where collection points were clearly visible. ___ In buildings where bins were hidden, the effect was negligible.

options.text: The results consequently depended on how the policy was implemented.
The policy was announced in winter.
The buildings had different window sizes.
Some bins were made of metal.

activities.explanation: The second sentence gives a contrasting implementation condition, so the gap should draw that conclusion.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence preserves the reference chain?
activities.passage: The room was used before presentations and complex negotiations. ___ Routine email, by contrast, was usually handled at shared desks.

options.text: These demanding tasks required a quiet space for preparation.
The desks were made of light wood.
The building opened in April.
The email system had recently changed.

activities.explanation: These demanding tasks refers to presentations and negotiations and explains the room's use.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which option completes the implementation report?
activities.passage: The audio-guide ratings were high. ___ The authors therefore avoid claiming that every visitor would value the guide equally.

options.text: Only visitors who chose to borrow it completed the evaluation.
The guide used three languages.
The museum opened in 1990.
The recordings were short.

activities.explanation: The self-selected sample explains the cautious conclusion.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence maintains the rhetorical structure?
activities.passage: The report begins by describing a fall in local shop numbers. ___ It then explains why a weekly market has brought some customers back.

options.text: The opening establishes the problem that the later example partially addresses.
The market sells bread and vegetables.
The report was written by a resident.
The shops are painted different colours.

activities.explanation: The gap should explain the role of the opening before the text moves to partial recovery.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence belongs in the community-centre gap?
activities.passage: The app's users reported saving time. ___ The authors recommend an independent trial before estimating the size of the benefit.

options.text: Those reports were based on personal estimates rather than timed tasks.
The app has a bright icon.
The users worked in three offices.
The trial was already independent.

activities.explanation: The measurement limitation motivates the recommendation for an independent trial.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence best completes the comparison?
activities.passage: The shared office reduced rent and encouraged informal contact. ___ Workers nevertheless reported fewer quiet periods for demanding tasks.

options.text: The financial saving was therefore accompanied by a working-condition cost.
The office had no shared equipment.
The rent increased after one month.
Demanding tasks disappeared.

activities.explanation: The missing sentence summarises the benefit and prepares the later limitation.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence fits the conclusion?
activities.passage: The council published the raw responses as well as its survey summary. ___ Residents could therefore inspect how the final claims had been formed.

options.text: It also described the method used to analyse them.
The survey was conducted in winter.
The council had three offices.
Residents were not invited to read it.

activities.explanation: The method is necessary for readers to understand how claims came from responses.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence preserves the argument's caution?
activities.passage: The mentoring trial improved attendance among participants who completed the first month. ___ The report avoids extending the result to all students.

options.text: It was unclear whether the most absent students had joined.
Every student completed the first month.
Attendance fell across the school.
The trial included no participants.

activities.explanation: Unknown participation explains why the result cannot be generalised.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence completes the policy analysis?
activities.passage: The policy worked in offices with visible collection points but had little effect where bins were hidden. ___ The recommendation therefore focuses on design as well as rules.

options.text: The contrast suggests that implementation shaped behaviour.
The policy was printed in large letters.
The offices all used identical furniture.
Rules were never mentioned.

activities.explanation: The difference between visible and hidden bins supports the implementation inference.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence fits the gap in the comparison?
activities.passage: The first design was cheaper to purchase. ___ The committee selected the second after considering costs over ten years.

options.text: The second was more durable and expected to require fewer repairs.
The first design had a wider entrance.
The committee did not discuss maintenance.
Both designs were discarded immediately.

activities.explanation: Durability and fewer repairs explain why long-term costs changed the decision.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence maintains the limitation?
activities.passage: The timetable reduced delays on two routes during its first month. ___ The team plans to monitor other routes before recommending a wider change.

options.text: This encouraging result is too narrow to establish a network-wide effect.
All routes had already improved equally.
The network was never measured.
The timetable was cancelled before testing.

activities.explanation: The first-month, two-route evidence explains the cautious next step.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the text.
activities.prompt: Which sentence completes the transparency argument?
activities.passage: The council published responses and its analytical method alongside the summary. ___ This made it possible to distinguish evidence from interpretation.

options.text: Readers could examine both the original material and the process used.
The council kept the questions private.
The summary contained no conclusions.
The responses were destroyed after publication.

activities.explanation: Access to the data and method explains how readers can separate evidence from interpretation.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the conclusion.
activities.prompt: Which sentence best completes the evidence paragraph?
activities.passage: The pilot attracted strong interest but demanded more staff time than predicted. ___ The organisers will continue it while redesigning registration.

options.text: The value of the idea is therefore clear, even though its process needs work.
No one wanted to participate.
Registration was already efficient.
The pilot has ended permanently.

activities.explanation: The gap balances demand with the administrative weakness before the continuation decision.
